title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases of Juveniles

articles.content_en: Article 1 Juvenile criminal cases as mentioned in this Interpretation refer to cases where the defendant has reached the age of fourteen but not the age of eighteen at the time of committing the alleged crime.

Article 2 The "age" as provided in Article 17 of the Criminal Law shall be calculated by the year, month and day of the Gregorian calendar, and shall be counted from the day following the birthday of the exact age.

Article 3 When adjudicating juvenile criminal cases, the age of the defendant at the time of committing the alleged crime shall be ascertained. The year, month and day of the defendant's birth shall be stated in the judgment document.

Article 4 Where there is insufficient evidence to prove that the defendant has reached the statutory age of criminal liability at the time of committing the alleged crime and it is truly impossible to ascertain the age, it shall be presumed that the defendant has not reached the corresponding statutory age of criminal liability.
Where relevant evidence is sufficient to prove that the defendant has reached the statutory age of criminal liability at the time of committing the alleged crime, but the exact date of birth of the defendant cannot be accurately ascertained, it shall be determined that the defendant has reached the corresponding statutory age of criminal liability.

Article 5 Where a person who has reached the age of fourteen but not the age of sixteen commits an act other than those provided in paragraph 2 of Article 17 of the Criminal Law, if such act simultaneously violates the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 17 of the Criminal Law, the crime shall be determined and the person shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 17 of the Criminal Law.

Article 6 Where a person who has reached the age of fourteen but not the age of sixteen occasionally engages in sexual acts with a young girl, if the circumstances are minor and no serious consequences are caused, it shall not be deemed as a crime.

Article 7 Where a person who has reached the age of fourteen but not the age of sixteen uses minor violence or threats to forcibly demand from another minor daily necessities, school supplies or money in a small amount carried by that minor, and no harmful consequences such as causing the victim to suffer from minor injury or above or being afraid to attend school or live normally have resulted, it shall not be deemed as a crime.
Where a person who has reached the age of sixteen but not the age of eighteen falls under the circumstances prescribed in the preceding paragraph, it shall generally not be deemed as a crime either.

Article 8 Where a person who has reached the age of sixteen but not the age of eighteen, out of bullying the weak or seeking spiritual stimulation, randomly assaults other minors, forcibly takes or demands property from other minors on multiple occasions, or arbitrarily damages public or private property, thereby disrupting the order of schools or other public places, if the circumstances are serious, the person shall be convicted and punished for the crime of picking quarrels and provoking trouble.

Article 10 Where a person who has reached the age of fourteen but not the age of sixteen commits theft, fraud or robbery of another person's property, and in order to conceal the stolen goods, resist arrest or destroy criminal evidence, uses violence on the spot, intentionally causing injury resulting in serious injury or death, or intentionally causing death, the person shall be convicted and punished respectively for the crime of intentional injury or the crime of intentional homicide.
Where a person who has reached the age of sixteen but not the age of eighteen commits the crime of theft, fraud or robbery, and in order to conceal the stolen goods, resist arrest or destroy criminal evidence, uses violence on the spot or threatens violence, the person shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provisions of Article 269 of the Criminal Law; if the circumstances are minor, the person may not be convicted and punished for the crime of robbery.

Article 11 When imposing penalties on juvenile offenders, full consideration shall be given to whether it is conducive to the education and correction of the juvenile offender.
When sentencing juvenile offenders, the provisions of Article 61 of the Criminal Law shall be followed, and full consideration shall be given to factors such as the motive and purpose of the minor's criminal act, the age at the time of the crime, whether it is the first crime, the expression of repentance after the crime, the personal growth experience and consistent behavior. For juvenile offenders who meet the applicable conditions for public surveillance, probation, a fine alone, or exemption from criminal punishment, public surveillance, probation, a fine alone, or exemption from criminal punishment shall be applied according to law.

Article 12 Where an actor commits acts harmful to society both before and after reaching the statutory age of criminal liability, only the criminal liability for the acts harmful to society committed after reaching the statutory age of criminal liability may be investigated according to law.
Where an actor commits different types of criminal acts before and after reaching the age of eighteen, the punishment for the crimes committed before the age of eighteen shall be given a lighter or mitigated punishment according to law. Where an actor commits the same type of criminal acts before and after reaching the age of eighteen, when sentencing, consideration shall be given to appropriately imposing a lighter or mitigated punishment for the crimes committed before the age of eighteen.

Article 13 Life imprisonment may only be applied to juvenile offenders whose crimes are extremely serious. Generally, life imprisonment shall not be imposed on a person who has reached the age of fourteen but not the age of sixteen.

Article 14 Except where the Criminal Law provides that deprivation of political rights "shall" be imposed as a supplementary punishment, juvenile offenders shall generally not be sentenced to deprivation of political rights as a supplementary punishment.
If juvenile offenders are sentenced to deprivation of political rights as a supplementary punishment, a lighter punishment shall be given according to law.
Where an offender who was a minor at the time of committing the alleged crime but has reached adulthood at the time of adjudication is sentenced to deprivation of political rights as a supplementary punishment, the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply.

Article 15 Where juvenile offenders commit crimes for which the Criminal Law provides that confiscation of property or a fine "shall" be imposed concurrently, the corresponding property penalty shall be imposed according to law; where juvenile offenders commit crimes for which the Criminal Law provides that confiscation of property or a fine "may" be imposed concurrently, the property penalty shall generally not be imposed.
When imposing a fine on a juvenile offender, a lighter or mitigated punishment shall be given according to law, and the amount of the fine shall be determined based on the circumstances of the crime, taking into comprehensive consideration the offender's ability to pay the fine. However, the minimum amount of the fine shall not be less than 500 yuan.
Where a juvenile offender who is sentenced to a fine is voluntarily paid the fine on his or her behalf by a guardian or other person, the People's Court shall permit it.

Article 18 With respect to commutation of punishment and parole for juvenile offenders, the standards may be appropriately relaxed according to law by reference to those for adult offenders.
Where a juvenile offender admits guilt and accepts the law, abides by prison regulations, and actively participates in study and labor, it may be deemed as "truly showing repentance", and commutation of punishment may be granted; the extent of commutation may be appropriately expanded, and the interval between commutations may be correspondingly shortened. If the provisions of paragraph 1 of Article 81 of the Criminal Law are met, parole may be granted.
Where a juvenile offender has reached adulthood during the service of sentence, the above provisions may apply to commutation of punishment and parole for such offender.

Article 19 Where a minor defendant in a criminal case with incidental civil action has personal property, the defendant shall bear the civil liability for compensation himself or herself; the insufficient part shall be compensated by the guardian, except where a unit acts as the guardian.
The defendant's compensation for the victim's material losses may be taken into consideration as a circumstance for sentencing.

Article 20 This Interpretation shall come into force as of the date of its promulgation.
The Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Juvenile Criminal Cases (Fa Fa [1995] No. 9) shall cease to be implemented as of the date of promulgation of this Interpretation.
